scientific_question: On independent consumed-Dev projects, does one real Official-path target-state failure cause a matched continuation to achieve more terminal EnvBench Official repairs than an equal continuation receiving typed-null feedback?
scope: Consumed Dev mechanism replication only. No protected Canary or Official Test access, representative effect estimate, SOTA claim, or leaderboard claim.

method.C0: One fresh gpt-5.6-sol xhigh continuous Agent session with an unrestricted construction shell emits one complete bootstrap program. A post-session execution of those exact bytes through the Spark EnvBench Official path produces either Pass, semantic Fail, or infrastructure censoring.
method.C1: For a valid semantic C0 Fail only, one tool-free native fork from the completed C0 session receives the typed-null replay schema and one revision opportunity.
method.T: For the same valid semantic C0 Fail, one tool-free native fork from the identical completed C0 session receives the real C0 Official-path public replay payload and one revision opportunity.
method.unique_causal_difference: Real target-state replay field values versus typed-null field values. Model, reasoning effort, completed parent prefix, output schema, disabled tools, revision count, and terminal executor are matched.

execution.construction_host_assignment: Odd positions use Spark; even positions use AgentHub. Assignment was recorded before outcomes and does not change within a case.
execution.target_state_executor: Spark RemoteEnvBenchProcessRunner for every project and arm
execution.source_cache: Exact-revision source only; no environment, candidate, result, or trajectory reuse.
execution.branch_order: Fixed alternating order in the case file.
execution.parallelism: At most one construction session per host and at most two simultaneous target-state executions on Spark.

eligibility_and_censoring.matched_branch_eligibility: C0 formed an admissible complete program and its exact bytes completed the Official-path executor with a semantic deployment nonpass.
eligibility_and_censoring.C0_pass: Record as a strong-Agent success and do not create C1 or T continuations.
eligibility_and_censoring.pre_candidate_failure: Record separately and do not create C1 or T continuations.
eligibility_and_censoring.infrastructure_failure: Retry the exact same program bytes up to three total attempts. Do not disclose a censored payload, regenerate a program, replace the project, or count it as semantic failure.
eligibility_and_censoring.postepisode: Execute C1 and T independently without returning results to either Agent. Apply the same three-attempt exact-program infrastructure policy.

analysis.primary_unit: Project with a valid semantic C0 Official-path nonpass and valid C1 and T terminal outcomes.
analysis.primary_contrast: T-exclusive Official wins versus C1-exclusive Official wins.
analysis.supporting_causal_chain: C0 exposes a concrete target-state counterexample, T changes the program correspondingly, T Official-passes, and C1 does not.
secondary: C0 Official Pass@1 and semantic-failure prevalence
generation, continuation, and target execution time
input, cached input, output, and reasoning tokens

decision_rule.promote_replay_into_core: At least two independent full supporting causal chains, more T-exclusive than C1-exclusive Official wins, and no target-executor fidelity contradiction.
decision_rule.retain_weak: Exactly one supporting causal chain with no C1-exclusive win; do not enter protected evaluation.
decision_rule.kill_replay_as_core: No supporting causal chain after at least four valid matched opportunities, or T-exclusive wins do not exceed C1-exclusive wins.
decision_rule.insufficient: Fewer than four valid matched opportunities; expand only with a new outcome-blind preregistered sample, without replacing projects.

safeguard_note: This preregistration adds no runtime hash, frozen contract, or gate. Git records the protocol and ordinary tests cover runner and executor parity.
